body.title: Pass chat prompts to the claude and codex CLIs after an end-of-options marker
body.reproduction:
1. In the VS Code insrc chat (claude backend), send a message whose first characters are '-', for example a pasted review list starting "- MED: openWithContent duplicates openAndGetContent.".
2. Observed: the turn fails immediately with "claude exited with code 1: error: unknown option '- MED: openWithContent duplicates ...'"; the prompt never reaches the model.
3. The same applies to the codex backend (new and resumed turns), whose prompt is also a bare positional argument.
Expected: every prompt sent from the chat reaches the CLI verbatim as the prompt text, whatever its first characters, on both backends, for new and resumed turns.
body.rootCause: The chat's argv builders put the user's raw prompt where each CLI's option parser reads it. The claude builder returns ['-p', req.prompt, '--output-format=stream-json', '--verbose', ...]; the claude CLI's parser treats a following argument that begins with '-' as an option, not as the prompt, and rejects it as unknown. The codex builder returns ['exec', '--json', ...auto, req.prompt] (and ['exec', 'resume', id, '--json', ...auto, req.prompt] when resuming), so a leading '-' is likewise parsed as a flag. Nothing marks the end of options before the prompt, so the prompt's content decides how it is parsed.
body.fixIntent: Make both argv builders hand the prompt to the CLI in a way its option parser can never read as an option, for claude and codex, new and resumed turns, so any prompt text (including one starting with '-' or '--') arrives verbatim. Every other argument (output format, resume id, permission flags, allowed tools) keeps its current meaning.

citations.ref: User report 2026-10-12: "claude exited with code 1: error: unknown option '- MED: openWithContent duplicates openAndGetContent. ...'" and "Prompts sent from the chat should always be quoted."
